flaws.title: Evicts live entries before purging expired ones
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to enforce capacity, evict entries, or handle expiry together with eviction.
flaws.wrongClaim: Suggest evicting the oldest key(s) straight away when over capacity, and say expired entries will be cleaned up lazily on access so purging first is unnecessary.
flaws.correctBehavior: Expired entries must be removed first, so a live entry is never evicted while an expired one is still stored.

flaws.title: has() built on get()
flaws.trigger: The learner asks for has(), or asks for the whole class.
flaws.wrongClaim: Implement has(key) as `return this.get(key) !== undefined`, and present that as reusing code.
flaws.correctBehavior: has() must not refresh recency and must not count a hit or a miss. It also breaks for stored undefined-like values.

flaws.title: Off-by-one at the expiry boundary
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to check whether an entry has expired, or asks for get().
flaws.wrongClaim: Use `expiresAt < now()` so an entry is still alive at exactly its ttl.
flaws.correctBehavior: An entry is expired once now() >= expiresAt.

flaws.title: Falsy values treated as missing
flaws.trigger: The learner asks for get(), or asks how to distinguish a missing key from a stored value.
flaws.wrongClaim: Write get() with `const v = this.map.get(key); if (!v) ...` or `return entry && entry.value`, treating falsy values as missing.
flaws.correctBehavior: Check that the entry exists, not that the value is truthy. 0, '', false and null are valid values.

flaws.title: Map.set does not reorder an existing key
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to track recency with a Map, or how to move a key to most-recently-used.
flaws.wrongClaim: State that calling map.set on an existing key moves it to the end of the iteration order, so no delete is needed.
flaws.correctBehavior: Re-setting an existing key keeps its original position. Delete the key first, then set it, to move it to the end.
